description: Holds 100 chords drawn from a 31-note scale tuned in whole number ratios and plays the selected one as polyphonic pitch and gate

params.text: Picks which of the five 31-note ratio scales the note buttons are tuned to
Moves every note of the current chord one step of the 31-note scale up
Moves every note of the current chord one octave up
Moves every note of the current chord one step of the 31-note scale down
Moves every note of the current chord one octave down
Picks which of the 100 chords is played and edited
Copies the notes of the current chord
Writes the copied notes into the current chord
While on, the chord is picked by hand and a cable in the Chord input no longer moves the selection

inputs.text: The notes of the chord as pitch, one note per channel, each note tuned by its ratio in the selected scale

outputs.text: The notes of the chord as pitch, one note per channel, each note tuned by its ratio in the selected scale
Carries 10V on the channel of every note that is on in the chord and 0V on the rest
A 10ms trigger on a note's channel when that note is switched on or when a chord change brings it in

notes: every one of the 100 chords comes up with no notes switched on, so nothing plays until keys are clicked on in the note grid
clicking a key in the note grid switches that note of the current chord on or off, and hovering a key shows the ratio it is tuned to
menu: Polyphonic Channels — sets how many channels the outputs carry, 1 to 16
Polyphony mode — lays the notes across the channels as Rotate, Reset or Reuse Note
Reorder — lays the notes of the current chord across the channels from lowest to highest
Auto Reorder — reorders the channels after every change, and the polyphony mode is then ignored
Auto Channels — gives the outputs only as many channels as there are notes switched on, and the Polyphonic Channels setting is then ignored
Insert Chord — pushes the chords after the current one along by one place and empties the current one; the hundredth chord is lost
Delete Chord — removes the current chord and pulls every later chord back one place
Round pattern input — rounds the voltage at the Chord input to the nearest chord in place of truncating it
